note: Everyday sentence pairs, nouns, places, names and numbers for the Talk screen. Written for this project; no phrasebook was copied. Hebrew is unpointed everyday spelling. Not yet checked by a native speaker.

fields.en: English wordings that mean this line (first is the one shown)
fields.he: Hebrew line; when the speaker's gender changes the words this is the man's form
fields.f: the same line said by a woman, when it differs
fields.toF: the same line said to a woman, when it differs
fields.alt: other Hebrew wordings that mean the same (matched when heard, never shown as the answer)
fields.g: noun gender for agreement: f feminine, p plural; masculine when absent
fields.pl: plural of a countable noun, used after a number
fields.verbs: to-forms that follow want, need and may I unchanged whoever speaks; thing = may be followed by a thing (buy a ticket)
fields.back: the English word to use when reading the Hebrew back, when the plain word belongs to another noun
fields.own: a noun that already says whose it is (my husband): no article is added
fields.food: the form used for the food in general (I do not eat fish)
fields.adjectives: m, f, mp, fp = masculine, feminine, masculine plural, feminine plural
fields.g values: f feminine, p plural, pf feminine plural; masculine when absent
